title.title: The BFSS threshold bound state, for every $N$
title.subtitle: Claim: SU($N$) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics has exactly one normalizable zero-energy state, for every $N \ge 2$

beats.text: Energy spectrum of the BFSS matrix model: a continuum starting at zero
Claim: exactly one normalizable state sits at the threshold, for every $N \ge 2$
Companion claim: for SU(2), infinitely many bound states inside the continuum

achievement.label: Witten (1995); BFSS matrix theory (1997)
achievement.context: Before: rigorous for SU(2) only (Sethi–Stern 1998); general $N$ by non-rigorous index counts
achievement.note: The SU(2) companion contradicts a statement in the original BFSS paper

verify.detail: No formalization; physicists should check the closure of the supercharge form
verify.ourCheck: We read the papers' claims and caveats; we did not referee them

sources.quote: Witten (1995) predicted the D0-brane threshold bound state
contradicts a statement in the original BFSS paper

plain: In matrix theory a graviton is a state sitting exactly at zero energy; this claims there is exactly one

steps: Add a mass term, where an index can count the states
Control what happens as particles cluster or separate
Remove the mass carefully: exactly one state survives

voice.text: The spectrum is a continuum from zero. Does a true state sit exactly there?
Add a mass and count states by an index, then remove the mass carefully.
Claimed: exactly one, for every N.
